```{r setup}
library(PhenotypeTemplates)
```

The templates in this package are built around a **disease of interest**: the
index event is a diagnosis (or the record of a condition in the observation
domain), and the other concept sets are clinical evidence that surrounds it.
An **active comparator new user (ACNU)** design inverts that: the index event
is a **drug exposure**, and the "disease of interest" role is played by the
treatment arm.

This article describes how to build ACNU drug exposure cohorts with these
templates, which parts of the design the templates express for you, and which
parts are study-design decisions you have to make before you generate any
cohort. It applies to drug-vs-drug comparisons that are **independent of any
outcome phenotype**: nothing here requires, or encodes, an outcome.

## What an ACNU design needs

An ACNU study has three elements, and only the first is a cohort definition:

1. **A new-user cohort per treatment arm.** A person enters the arm on the
   first date on which they started *that* drug after a clean period with no
   exposure to *that* drug.
2. **A new-user cohort of the comparator.** The same, for the alternative
   treatment.
3. **The outcome.** A separate cohort definition, applied to both arms.

The new-user restriction is per arm, not per study. A person who is a new
user of both arms can be a new user of either; which arm they are attributed
to is decided by the study design (typically the arm they actually started),
not by the phenotype. Building both arms symmetrically is what makes them
comparable, and it is why the outcome must stay out of both definitions.

## Mapping the design onto the buckets

The bucket that does the work is `I`: it is the index event. Every ACNU arm
is described as:

| Template input | ACNU meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `I` | **the drug exposure of that arm** (the new-user entry event) |
| `S`, `D`, `C`, `E` | not used: they would encode indication or morbidities, which differ between arms by construction |
| `T` | not used: it would be the comparator, i.e. study design, not phenotype |
| `A` | not used as an exclusion of the drug; alternatives are arm questions, not phenotype questions |

The consequence is deliberate: **an ACNU arm cohort uses only the `I` bucket,
and therefore only the `L0` evidence level is generated**. Supplying `S`,
`D`, `T`, `C`, `E` or `A` for an ACNU arm does not make the phenotype better;
it reintroduces the confounding the active comparator is there to remove, and
it can never be symmetric between arms.

```{r ladder-consequence}
config <- phenotypeConfig(
  clinicalCourse = "persistent_stable",
  expectedCareSetting = "outpatient_expected"
)
config$hasDescreteRecordedSymptoms <- FALSE
config$requiresActiveTreatmentWithin30d <- FALSE
config$expectsConditionSpecificFollowupOrSequelae1yr <- FALSE
config$requiresDiagnosticTestOrProcedure <- FALSE
c(
  symptoms = config$hasDescreteRecordedSymptoms,
  diagnostics = config$requiresDiagnosticTestOrProcedure,
  treatment = config$requiresActiveTreatmentWithin30d,
  followup = config$expectsConditionSpecificFollowupOrSequelae1yr
)
```

## Building one arm

Each arm is one call. The two arms of a comparison are separate calls, with
the same `config` and different `I`:

```{r arms, eval = FALSE}
# Arm 1: new users of the DOAC arm
doacArm <- buildPhenotypeTemplates(
  conceptSets = list(I = csDoac),
  phenotypeLabel = "Apixaban or rivaroxaban new users",
  config = acnuConfig
)

# Arm 2: new users of warfarin
warfarinArm <- buildPhenotypeTemplates(
  conceptSets = list(I = csWarfarin),
  phenotypeLabel = "Warfarin new users",
  config = acnuConfig,
  startCohortId = max(doacArm$cohortId)
)
```

Use `startCohortId` so the two arms get disjoint cohort IDs; the two sets can
then be `rbind()`ed into a single cohort definition set for
`CohortGenerator`.

## Choosing the clinical course for an arm

The clinical course controls the index event limit and the cohort exit, and
for an ACNU arm both should follow the **treatment**, not the disease:

* `persistent_stable` produces a first-occurrence index (`expressionLimit =
  "First"`) and exits at the end of continuous observation. This is the
  conventional choice for a "first new use of the drug, followed forward"
  arm.
* `transient_recurrent` produces `expressionLimit = "All"`, i.e. one
  qualifying event per exposure episode. That is a new-episode design, not a
  new-user design, and the two arms are no longer risk-set comparable unless
  every episode in both arms is handled the same way.

For a new-user design, prefer `persistent_stable` with an explicit age
restriction, and keep the same `config` for both arms.

## The clean window is a design decision

The templates make the first-occurrence restriction and the observation
window configurable, but they do not decide how long the clean period before
the index should be. That is the single most consequential decision in an
ACNU study, because a clean period that is longer in one arm than the other
changes who can enter each arm.

Record the clean window you used next to the cohorts you generated, and apply
the same one to both arms. If an arm needs a different clean window (for
example because the drug is only recently available), say so explicitly
rather than letting it differ silently:

```{r clean-window}
acnuDesign <- data.frame(
  arm = c("DOAC", "Warfarin"),
  indexConceptSet = c("Apixaban or rivaroxaban", "Warfarin"),
  cleanWindowDays = c(365L, 365L),
  minAgeYears = c(18L, 18L),
  maxAgeYears = c(NA_integer_, NA_integer_),
  clinicalCourse = "persistent_stable",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
acnuDesign
```

## Age and sex restrictions belong to the comparison

An age or sex restriction on one arm only makes the arms non-exchangeable.
Set `minAge`, `maxAge`, `male` and `female` once and reuse that `config` for
both arms, as above, rather than configuring each arm separately.

## What is intentionally not here

* **No outcome logic.** The outcome cohort is applied to both arms by the
  study design, not by these templates. A cohort definition that includes the
  outcome is not an ACNU phenotype; it is an outcome-restricted cohort, and
  it cannot be used as a comparator.
* **No indication restriction.** Restricting both arms to a shared
  indication is legitimate and often necessary, but it is a separate
  decision. If you need it, add the indication as an additional, *identical*
  restriction to both arms, and document it alongside `acnuDesign`. Do not
  express it through the `A` bucket, which excludes rather than restricts.

## Provenance

Keep `acnuDesign` with the generated cohort definitions. Together with the
concept sets it is everything needed to know which two populations were
compared, how they were made new users, and how they were indexed, which is
the part of an ACNU study that cannot be recovered from the cohort SQL
afterwards.
